page: Amazon Web Services m7gd.16xlarge is a general-purpose server powered by the AWS Graviton processor family. It features 64 dedicated physical cores built on the arm64 ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 architecture, running at 2.6 GHz with a 1.0 thread-per-core ratio. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes 3800 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 30 Gbps, managed via the Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core and memory performance. The server achieved a top-tier rating in Geekbench multi-core testing and software compilation, alongside a top-tier PassMark memory score. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching 253.41 GB/sec for large block read-only operations and 121.54 GB/sec for large block write operations. Multi-core stress-ng performance is rated strong, while single-core performance remains in the average tier.

This hardware profile is optimized for workloads requiring a balance of compute, memory, and high-speed local storage. The inclusion of 3800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage combined with strong database operation benchmarks makes it highly suitable for relational databases, Redis key-value stores, and static web serving. The Arm-based architecture offers high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for multi-threaded applications, software compilation, and medium-model LLM text generation, though single-threaded tasks and small-model text generation show lower relative performance.
